slides.heading: Continuous Median
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Heaps
slides.narration: Let's solve Continuous Median, a hard heaps problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Insert numbers one at a time and query the running median, using a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Insert numbers one at a time and query the running median, using a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Keep the smaller half in a max-heap and the larger half in a min-heap, balanced in size.
slides.narration: Keep the smaller half in a max-heap and the larger half in a min-heap, balanced in size.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Keep a sorted list, insert in place → O(n) per insert
Two heaps (max-heap low, min-heap high) → O(log n) insert, O(1) median
slides.narration: Inserting into a sorted list is linear each time. Two heaps, a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper, give log n inserts and constant-time median.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Rebalance so sizes differ by at most one
3. Median is the top of the bigger heap or the average of tops
slides.narration: Step by step. First, insert into the right heap. Second, rebalance so sizes differ by at most one. Third, median is the top of the bigger heap or the average of tops.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Insert adds to the lower heap if empty or smaller than its top, otherwise upper. Then we move one element if sizes differ by two, and compute the median from the tops.

slides.heading: Complexity
bullets: Time: O(log n) insert, O(1) median
slides.narration: Time is O of log n insert, constant median. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Rebalance after every insert, and average the two tops when the sizes are equal.
